result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers spot that the symmetric 4px spacing leaves group titles floating between groups. Both recommend roughly 24px between groups with a tighter gap between a title and its items, and both remove the per-item borders. A wins because it ties the larger padding to click and tap targets, and adds label styling for titles and a focus ring. B uses a clean 4px scale and flex gap, but it treats the sidebar as pointer-only and says less about tap targets. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers spot the same core problem: every gap is 4px, so group titles float between groups. Both also recommend about 24px between groups, removing the per-item borders, 8px/12px item padding and concrete CSS. B is slightly better: it ties the padding directly to click-target size and legibility, makes titles read as labels through type styling, and keeps keyboard focus visible. A's strengths are its explicit 4px scale and its cleaner use of `gap` on the parent.
